context: The balance factor is the height of the left subtree minus the height of the right. A leaf has height 0 and an empty subtree has height −1. A tree is balanced only if the absolute value of every node's balance factor is at most 1. The factors below follow from the connections in the figure.

This example uses an ordinary binary search tree with no rotations to maintain balance. The three panels contain 3, 4, and 5 nodes, respectively, and are labeled “Perfect binary tree,” “Balanced binary tree,” and “Binary tree.” Leaf 5 remains the right child of root 4 throughout.
prose.result: A tree can cease to be perfect and still be balanced. An AVL tree uses rotations to restore balance after insertion.

steps.announcement: The initial perfect binary tree has root 4, left child 3, and right child 5.
steps.explanation: Root 4 initially has leaves 3 and 5 as its left and right children. These 3 nodes fill two levels, and every node has balance factor 0. The tree is both perfect and balanced.
steps.key_state: Root 4 initially has left child 3 and right child 5. All three nodes have balance factor 0.
steps.title: Initial perfect binary tree

steps.announcement: Insert 2 to the left of 3. The tree is no longer perfect, but nodes 4 and 3 both have balance factor 1, so it remains balanced.
steps.explanation: Insert 2. It is less than both 4 and 3, so it becomes the left child of 3. Root 4 now has left child 3 and right child 5, and 3 has only a left child, 2. Nodes 2 and 5 are leaves. There are 4 nodes. Nodes 4 and 3 both have balance factor 1, so the tree is still balanced although it is no longer perfect.
steps.key_state: After inserting 2, root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5, and 3 has left child 2. Both 4 and 3 have balance factor 1, so the tree remains balanced.
steps.title: The tree remains balanced after inserting 2

steps.announcement: Insert 1 to the left of 2. The balance factors of node 3 and root 4 both become 2.
steps.explanation: Insert 1. Follow the leftward path 4 → 3 → 2 and attach 1 to the left of 2. The left chain is now 4 → 3 → 2 → 1, and root 4 also has a right leaf, 5, for a total of 5 nodes. Node 3 has left and right subtree heights 1 and −1, and root 4 has heights 2 and 0. Both balance factors are now 2, so the tree is unbalanced.
steps.key_state: After inserting 1, the left chain is 4 → 3 → 2 → 1, and root 4 has right leaf 5. Both 3 and 4 have balance factor 2.
steps.title: Inserting 1 unbalances the tree

prose.summary: Successive insertions on the same side lengthen a branch one level at a time until a previously balanced binary tree no longer meets the balance condition.
prose.title: Insertion can unbalance a search tree
